successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: the whole kingdom, annexed by Claudius as the province of Thracia in AD 46

rulers.name: Cotys III and Rhescuporis II (divided kingdom)

ledger.x: 87-85 BC: Thracian raids into Roman Macedonia with Mithridates.
85 BC: the Mithridatic war ends with the Peace of Dardanos; the raids lapse on the pages.
31 BC: the Sapaean house takes the whole kingdom.

ledger.cp: Bessi (Rhodope tribe under the priest Vologaesus)

ledger.x: 11 BC: the second Bessi rising fails; 'Roman expansion along the Danube followed the Bessi revolt'.
ledger.cp: Bessi (Rhodope tribe under the priest Vologaesus)

ledger.x: AD 21: the rebellion 'failed' within the year.
AD 46: Claudius ends the revolt and the kingdom together.

AD 46: 'In 46 AD, Roman Emperor Claudius put an end to the kingdom by annexing it' and 'made Thracia into a Roman province'; the Odrysian page: 'The Romans dissolved the Sapaean kingdom in 45/6 and made it the province of Thracia'.

wars.name: Thracian raids on Roman Macedonia (First Mithridatic War)
wars.outcome: Roman victory in the wider war (Dardanos, 85); the raids leave no border change

wars.name: Bessi revolt of Vologaesus
wars.outcome: the Thracian king killed (13); the second rising of 11 'unsuccessful'; Roman expansion along the Danube follows

wars.name: Thracian revolt of AD 21
wars.outcome: the rebellion 'failed'; Rhoemetalces II kept at Philippopolis

wars.name: Thracian revolt of AD 44-46 and annexation
wars.outcome: Rhoemetalces III killed; Claudius annexes the kingdom as the province of Thracia (46)

certainty.note: A client kingdom of tribes under a Hellenized court: the Haemus, the Danube and the Hebrus are the only lines the pages name.
